parts.persona: Act as an experienced Scottish Primary teacher specialising in concrete-pictorial-abstract numeracy approaches.
parts.act: Create three hands-on classroom station activities and a teacher questioning script
parts.recipient: for a mixed-ability Primary 4 class working at Curriculum for Excellence First Level, including pupils who benefit from visual scaffolds
parts.theme: exploring equivalent halves, quarters, and eighths using everyday classroom and food-sharing contexts.
parts.structure: Present the output as a clear table with columns for Station Name, Equipment Needed, Pupil Instructions (in child-friendly language), and two Hinge Questions to check understanding.

parts.persona: Act as a Primary Literacy Coordinator skilled in inclusive writing pedagogy.
parts.act: Generate an imaginative story starter alongside a tiered vocabulary word bank
parts.recipient: for Primary 5 pupils transitioning from First to Second Level, including reluctant writers who struggle to start a paragraph
parts.theme: set around discovering a hidden sea cave along the Scottish coastline during a storm.
parts.structure: Provide a 60-word atmospheric opening hook, followed by three bulleted lists of sensory words (Sight, Sound, Movement) and three sentence stems to help pupils write the next paragraph.

parts.persona: Act as a Curriculum for Excellence Interdisciplinary Learning (IDL) specialist.
parts.act: Design a structured classroom role-play debate resource
parts.recipient: for Primary 7 pupils working securely at Second Level
parts.theme: evaluating a proposal to build an offshore wind farm near a coastal Scottish fishing and tourism community.
parts.structure: Organise into four stakeholder role cards (Local Fisherman, Renewable Engineer, Marine Conservationist, Community Councillor), each containing three key arguments and one question to ask another group.

parts.persona: Act as a Scottish secondary Computing Science teacher focused on computational thinking and resilience.
parts.act: Write three short pseudocode scenarios containing deliberate logical errors
parts.recipient: for S2 pupils working at Third Level who understand basic loops and selection (`if/else`) statements
parts.theme: based on score-tracking and collision detection in a simple retro arcade game.
parts.structure: For each challenge, display the flawed pseudocode block, a subtle pupil hint that avoids giving away the answer, and a collapsible teacher solution explaining the bug.

parts.persona: Act as a secondary History teacher experienced in literacy differentiation across mixed-attainment classes.
parts.act: Write an informative reading passage in two differentiated reading tiers, accompanied by comprehension questions
parts.recipient: for an S3 History class spanning Third Level and Fourth Level literacy skills
parts.theme: explaining living and working conditions in 19th-century Scottish industrial tenements.
parts.structure: Provide Version A (accessible sentences with a 5-word glossary in a two-column table) and Version B (incorporating advanced historical vocabulary), followed by three stepped questions covering literal, inferential, and evaluative skills.

parts.persona: Act as a secondary Biology teacher specialising in practical scientific inquiry.
parts.act: Draft a pre-lab prediction starter and a post-lab formative exit ticket
parts.recipient: for S3 Biology pupils working at Fourth Level preparing to transition into Senior Phase
parts.theme: investigating the effect of temperature on catalase enzyme activity using potato tissue and hydrogen peroxide.
parts.structure: Format as a 5-minute starter prompt asking pupils to identify independent, dependent, and control variables, followed by a 3-question Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) exit ticket.

parts.persona: Act as a Qualifications Scotland National 5 Applications of Mathematics assessor and classroom practitioner.
parts.act: Create three realistic multi-step numeracy context questions with worked marking guidance
parts.recipient: for S4 and S5 pupils revising for their National 5 Applications of Mathematics exam
parts.theme: calculating gross pay, overtime rates, National Insurance deductions, and monthly savings goals from a part-time retail job.
parts.structure: Present each question with realistic data tables, mark allocations in brackets, and a step-by-step worked solution highlighting where method marks are awarded.

parts.persona: Act as a Scottish secondary English teacher experienced in Senior Phase close reading skills.
parts.act: Write an original non-fiction persuasive extract and four analysis questions
parts.recipient: for S4 pupils practising National 5 Reading for Understanding, Analysis and Evaluation (RUAE)
parts.theme: exploring the impact of smartphone habits on teenage sleep and attention spans.
parts.structure: Provide a 250-word journalism-style passage with numbered paragraphs, four 'Explain how the writer's language...' questions (2 to 4 marks each), and a bulleted 'Quote + Comment' marking guide.

parts.persona: Act as a Qualifications Scotland Higher Computing Science teacher.
parts.act: Develop a low-stakes diagnostic retrieval quiz covering common exam misconceptions
parts.recipient: for S5 and S6 Higher Computing Science candidates revising Software Design and Development
parts.theme: focusing on parameter passing (by value vs by reference), local and global variables, and standard algorithms (linear search, find minimum/maximum, count occurrences).
parts.structure: Create 6 short-answer and code-tracing questions, followed by a concise marking key that explicitly flags typical candidate pitfalls.

parts.persona: Act as a Scottish Higher History specialist focusing on analytical essay writing.
parts.act: Produce an essay planning scaffold that contrasts isolated factor descriptions with sustained analytical evaluation
parts.recipient: for S5 and S6 pupils aiming to move from descriptive paragraphs to Higher-standard evaluation
parts.theme: assessing the relative importance of factors leading to the outbreak of the First World War (alliances, naval rivalry, imperialism, and domestic tensions).
parts.structure: Format as a side-by-side comparison showing one weak narrative paragraph versus one high-scoring analytical paragraph, followed by four reusable evaluative linking phrases.
